interest: This document offers a valuable window into interwar international commercial law, trademark protection, and cross-border industrial relations between the United States and Japan. It illustrates the global reach of commercial friction, such as Japanese manufactured goods being deceptively marketed under American pretenses in Egypt, and the unauthorized use of prominent American brand names like Underwood for refurbished typewriters in Yokohama. Furthermore, the entry regarding J. A. Bertsch highlights the practical financial and legal difficulties American inventors faced regarding technology transfers and foreign exchange controls on dollar-denominated royalty remittances from Japan.
overview: This document is a Department of State List of Papers (docket sheet) for decimal file 894.543, recording correspondence and administrative actions concerning intellectual and industrial property, trademark disputes, and commercial licensing involving Japan. The sheet indexes entries 46 through 49, highlighting diverse legal and commercial matters: correspondence with The M. Stein Cosmetic Company; a complaint forwarded via the Department of Commerce regarding the fraudulent marketing of Japanese barber chairs as American products in Alexandria, Egypt; trademark opposition by the Underwood Elliott Fisher Company against an application by the Takemori Typewriter Company in Yokohama for 'Master Grade Remanufactured Underwood'; and an inquiry from J. A. Bertsch of St. Louis seeking guidance on receiving U.S. dollar royalty remittances from a Japanese chemical firm licensing his process.

subfiles.about: A Department of State docket sheet indexing incoming and outgoing correspondence regarding Japanese trademark disputes, fraudulent country-of-origin labeling, and patent royalty remittances.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet lists documents 46 through 49 registered under Department of State decimal file 894.543 relating to patents, trade names, and trademarks. It records a communication with The M. Stein Cosmetic Co., an investigation request regarding Japanese-made barber chairs marketed as American in Egypt, trademark opposition proceedings concerning 'Master Grade Remanufactured Underwood' typewriters registered by Takemori Typewriter Co. in Yokohama, and an inquiry from J. A. Bertsch concerning dollar-denominated royalty payments from a Japanese chemical firm. Notations indicate routing through the Office of the Legal Adviser (LE) and the Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE).
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers (File 894.543)
